# Cross-SDK capability matrix

_Load this before finalizing any plan (SKILL.md Step 5) so the plan only contains things the target SDK can actually do._

This file answers one question: **is this recommendation possible on the SDK this project uses?** It does not explain how to implement anything. For that, load the SDK reference for the project's target: `unity_sdk_reference.md`, `unreal_sdk_reference.md`, `visionos_sdk_reference.md`, `androidxr_sdk_reference.md`, or `webxr_sdk_reference.md`.

The strategy in `data_strategy.md` and the archetype playbooks in `playbooks.md` are deliberately SDK-neutral, which means they will happily suggest something the target SDK does not support. This file is the screen that catches it.

**Two column headings name a toolchain, not a device.** "visionOS" means a native Swift app; a Unity app shipped to Vision Pro is in the Unity column. "Android XR" means the native Kotlin SDK; a Unity or Unreal app on an Android headset is in its engine's column. "C++" means the standalone C++ SDK for custom engines; C++ written against the Unreal plugin is in the Unreal column.

---

## The one hard platform limit

**visionOS exposes no eye tracking to applications.** Apple does not provide eye-tracking rays to apps, so the visionOS SDK records HMD forward direction as the gaze signal. Everything downstream of that — heatmaps, dwell, gaze objectives, "what did they look at" — measures head orientation on this platform and eye attention on eye-tracked hardware elsewhere.

No SDK release changes this. When a plan's core question is about eye attention and the target is Vision Pro, the answer is to reframe the question, not to instrument harder. This is the only entry in this file that is a property of the hardware platform rather than of an SDK's maturity.

---

## Primitive availability

What an integration records or configures deliberately: the instrumentation primitives a tracking plan is built from (events, properties, sensors, dynamic objects, gaze, surveys), the platform features around them, and the upload workflows that feed replay. Each cell says whether the SDK offers the thing at all, and with what limitation.

| Primitive | Unity | Unreal | visionOS | Android XR | WebXR | C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Custom events | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes, requires a position argument | yes, requires a position argument |
| Typed event properties | yes | **C++ only; the Blueprint variant stringifies every value** | **no**, string-only dictionary, no typed alternative | yes | yes | yes, JSON properties keep their types |
| Event property count | yes, unlimited | yes, unlimited | yes, unlimited | **10 per event, surplus dropped silently** | yes, unlimited | yes, unlimited |
| Session properties | yes | yes | yes, typed | yes | yes | yes, string, int and float overloads |
| Participant identity | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes, `SetUserName` / `SetDeviceName`; no participant namespace |
| Participant properties | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | **no**, no participant API; use session properties |
| Session tags | yes | yes | **not documented** | **not documented** | yes | **no** |
| Session name | yes | yes | **not documented** | **not documented** | yes | yes |
| Sensors (custom) | yes | yes, float only | verify live | yes, float only | yes | yes, float only |
| Sensors (automatic) | yes, broad | **opt-in components** | **narrow, see below** | **FPS only** | **moderate** | **no**, none; the host pushes everything |
| Dynamic objects | yes | yes | yes | yes | **Three.js and Mattercraft only** | yes |
| Dynamic object linked to an event | yes, parameter | yes, parameter | yes, parameter | **by property convention** | yes, parameter | yes, parameter |
| ID pools for spawned objects | yes | yes, Id Pool Asset | **no**, register each instance at spawn | **no**, register each instance at spawn | **no**, register each instance at spawn | **no**, register each instance with a custom id |
| Gaze stream | yes | yes | **head direction only** | yes, when `enable_gaze` is set | yes | **host-supplied; eye-tracked or head ray is the host's choice** |
| Per-object gaze and heatmaps | yes | yes | **head-direction based** | yes | **Three.js and Mattercraft only** | **host must raycast and report the hit object** |
| Eye-tracked fixations | yes, on supported hardware | yes, via Fixation Recorder | **no**, never; Apple exposes no eye-tracking rays to apps | verify live | **hardware dependent** | **host computes fixations; the SDK only records them** |
| Objectives | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| ExitPoll | yes, UI shipped | yes, UMG widgets shipped | yes, SwiftUI views shipped | **not documented** | **no UI provided; build the survey yourself** | **no UI provided; voice answers supported** |
| ExitPoll offline | verify live | verify live | yes, question sets cached | **n/a**, no ExitPoll | **no** | **no** |
| Scene upload | yes, in-engine tools | yes, in-engine tools | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App |
| Dynamic object mesh upload | yes, in-engine tools | yes, Dynamic Object Manager | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App | yes, Upload Web App |
| Local cache / offline upload | yes | yes | yes, well specified | **not documented** | **not documented** | **no**, host must persist failed requests itself |
| Remote controls | yes | yes | **not documented** | **not documented** | **not documented** | **no** |
| Media and 360 | yes | yes | **not documented** | **not documented** | **not documented** | **media gaze overload only** |
| Multiplayer | yes, components | yes, Lobby IDs | **not documented** | **not documented** | **`setLobbyId` only** | **`SetLobbyId` only** |
| Audio recording | yes | **not documented** | **ExitPoll voice only** | **not documented** | **not documented** | **ExitPoll voice only** |
| Active Session View | yes | yes | **not documented** | **not documented** | **no** | **not documented** |
| Ready Room | yes | **no** | **no** | **no** | **no** | **no** |
| LMS forwarding | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

"Not documented" means the feature has no page in that SDK's docs section. Treat it as unavailable for planning purposes, and verify live before telling a team either way. Absence is weakest evidence on the newest SDKs, visionOS and Android XR. "Verify live" means the row has not been checked for that SDK yet.

**What each row means**

- **Custom events**: A named, timestamped event the app sends from its own logic, with optional properties and a world position. The unit of behavioral instrumentation.
- **Typed event properties**: Whether an event's property values keep their type (number, boolean, string) on the wire. A numeric property can only be averaged, charted or filtered numerically if it arrives as a number.
- **Event property count**: How many key-value properties one event may carry before the SDK drops the surplus.
- **Session properties**: Key-value facts that describe one whole session: app version, device mode, experimental condition, environment. The basis for filtering and cohort comparison.
- **Participant identity**: A stable identifier for the person (participant id, optionally a display name), so sessions from the same person can be joined across devices and over time. Identity only; attributes are the next row.
- **Participant properties**: Key-value attributes of the person that persist across their sessions: role, cohort, experience level, age band, height. They live on the participant profile, not on each session.
- **Session tags**: Labels the SDK attaches to a session at runtime for grouping, such as a build flavour or cohort. Analysts can also tag sessions on the dashboard after the fact, which needs no SDK support.
- **Session name**: A human-readable name for a session, set from the app and shown in session lists instead of the generated id.
- **Sensors (custom)**: A continuous numeric value the app samples over time under a sensor name: heart rate, load, speed. Charted on the session timeline, with per-session average, minimum and maximum queryable.
- **Sensors (automatic)**: The set of sensor streams the SDK records on its own, such as frame rate, battery and head orientation. The automatic capture table below lists them row by row.
- **Dynamic objects**: An object in the scene registered with the SDK so its position, rotation, and per-object gaze and interaction are recorded and it is drawn in replay. Needs its mesh uploaded separately.
- **Dynamic object linked to an event**: How a custom event names the dynamic object it concerns: a parameter on the event call, or a property the team sets by convention.
- **ID pools for spawned objects**: SDK-managed pools of reusable ids for objects spawned at runtime, so transient instances aggregate without the app inventing ids.
- **Gaze stream**: The continuous record of where the user is looking: head pose plus a gaze direction or hit point, sampled about ten times a second. Heatmaps, dwell and attention metrics are computed from it.
- **Per-object gaze and heatmaps**: Gaze attributed to a specific dynamic object, with hit positions in that object's own space. Enables per-object dwell, attention and heatmaps.
- **Eye-tracked fixations**: Fixations detected from eye-tracking data: gaze held on a point for a minimum duration, as distinct from head direction. Needs eye-tracking hardware and a fixation detector.
- **Objectives**: Dashboard-defined success logic composed of steps over events, gaze and survey answers, scored per session. A platform feature, so it works on any SDK once the inputs exist.
- **ExitPoll**: In-app surveys whose question sets are managed on the dashboard and fetched by hook name at runtime. The row also says whether the SDK ships the survey UI.
- **ExitPoll offline**: Whether question sets are cached so a survey can run, and queue its answers, without a network connection.
- **Scene upload**: How the scene geometry that replay and heatmaps are drawn on reaches the platform: in-engine export tooling, or the Upload Web App.
- **Dynamic object mesh upload**: How a registered object's mesh reaches the platform so it is drawn in replay. Always a separate step from scene upload.
- **Local cache / offline upload**: Whether the SDK stores session data locally when an upload fails and retries later, so offline or flaky-network sessions survive.
- **Remote controls**: Dashboard-managed variables the app reads at session start, for feature flags and A/B assignment without a new build.
- **Media and 360**: Recording gaze against uploaded 360 video or images, with media time and texture coordinates, so attention on media content is measurable.
- **Multiplayer**: Linking sessions that share a multiplayer lobby so they can be analyzed together. The row says whether the SDK ships anything beyond a lobby id.
- **Audio recording**: Capturing microphone audio, either into the session or as an ExitPoll voice answer.
- **Active Session View**: Watching a session's data arrive on the dashboard while the session is still running.
- **Ready Room**: A pre-session readiness check the SDK can run before the experience starts: eye-tracking calibration, controllers, boundary.
- **LMS forwarding**: Forwarding objective and session outcomes to a learning management system. A platform integration configured on the dashboard.

## Automatic capture differences

What the SDK records on its own once a session is running, with no instrumentation. The planning question for these rows is whether a metric is free, opt-in, host-supplied, or absent, because every "no" here is a row the team has to record itself or go without.

Every SDK except C++ captures some base layer with no instrumentation (see `queryable_data.md`, which is written from Unity's behaviour). The C++ SDK captures nothing on its own: every row below is something the host pushes in, or absent. Where they differ:

| Automatic capture | Unity | Unreal | visionOS | Android XR | WebXR | C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session lifecycle events | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Head pose / position | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | **host-supplied via `RecordGaze`** |
| Head pitch | yes | **component** | yes | verify live | yes | verify live |
| Head yaw | yes | **component** | **v1.0.1+, off by default** | verify live | yes | verify live |
| Head roll | yes | verify live | **no**, not recorded | verify live | verify live | verify live |
| Gaze | yes | yes, via Player Tracker | **head direction** | yes, when enabled | yes | **host-supplied** |
| Hands | yes | yes | yes, when `isHandTrackingRequired` | yes | yes | **no** |
| Controllers | yes | yes | **n/a**, no controllers | yes | yes | **host-registered dynamic objects** |
| FPS | yes | **component** | yes | yes | yes | **no** |
| Battery | yes | **component** | yes | verify live | **no** | **no** |
| Participant height | verify live | **component** | yes, `c3d.participant.height` | verify live | **no** | **no** |
| Boundary / room size | yes | **component** | **n/a**, no boundary on this platform | verify live | **`bounded-floor` only** | **no** |
| Draw calls, memory, main thread | yes | **no** | verify live | **no** | **renderer passed in only** | **no** |
| Biometrics | yes, on supported hardware | **integration dependent** | **no** | **no** | **no** | **no**, only via `RecordSensor` |
| Editor sessions excluded | yes | **behind a dashboard toggle** | **no**, no equivalent | **no**, no equivalent | **no**, no equivalent | **no**, no equivalent |

Three rows change a Phase 1 recommendation:

- **"Component" is not "automatic."** On Unreal, most comfort, performance and boundary metrics come from built-in components the team adds. Name the component.
- **Android XR documents only FPS as automatic**, and visionOS is narrow too, though it gives participant height for free, which nothing else does.
- **Only Unity filters developer sessions.** On every other target, explicit `development_mode` separation is required rather than advisory.
- **C++ captures nothing.** "Host-supplied" in that column means the row exists only if the host engine calls the SDK with the data every frame; plan it as engine work, not as instrumentation.

**What each row means**

- **Session lifecycle events**: Session start and end, with timestamps and duration, recorded without instrumentation.
- **Head pose / position**: The headset's world position and rotation over time. The basis of the path drawn in replay.
- **Head pitch**: Head pitch, looking up or down, recorded as a sensor stream.
- **Head yaw**: Head yaw, turning left or right, recorded as a sensor stream.
- **Head roll**: Head roll, tilting the head sideways, recorded as a sensor stream.
- **Gaze**: The gaze stream recorded without the app calling anything. See the gaze stream row above for what it contains.
- **Hands**: Hand-tracking poses recorded when the platform provides them.
- **Controllers**: Controller poses and button or axis input, recorded as dynamic objects.
- **FPS**: Frame rate sampled as a sensor. The input to the FPS and comfort scores.
- **Battery**: Device battery level sampled as a sensor.
- **Participant height**: The user's eye height estimated from the headset and stored as a participant property.
- **Boundary / room size**: The size of the play area or guardian boundary, and boundary-crossing events.
- **Draw calls, memory, main thread**: Rendering and system load: draw calls, memory use and main-thread time, sampled as sensors.
- **Biometrics**: Heart rate, skin response, pupil diameter and similar signals from supported hardware, recorded as sensors.
- **Editor sessions excluded**: Whether sessions recorded inside the engine editor are kept out of dashboard analytics automatically.

## Which business questions each SDK can carry

Derived from the primitive table: a question is "yes" on an SDK only when every feature it needs is supported there. Where it is not, the cell names the feature that limits it, so the plan can substitute or reframe. Use this with the business question map in `data_strategy.md`, which says what to add; this table says whether the target can carry it.

| Business question | Unity | Unreal | visionOS | Android XR | WebXR | C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where do users drop out during onboarding? | yes | **partial**: Typed event properties | **no**: Typed event properties | yes | yes | yes |
| Which step causes learners to fail? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Which content gets completed, repeated, or abandoned? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Which objects attract attention but not action? | yes | yes | **partial**: Per-object gaze and heatmaps | yes | **partial**: Dynamic objects, Per-object gaze and heatmaps | **partial**: Per-object gaze and heatmaps |
| Are users getting lost? | yes | yes | **partial**: Gaze stream | yes | **partial**: Dynamic objects | **partial**: Gaze stream |
| Which mechanic is actually being used? | yes | **partial**: Typed event properties | **no**: Typed event properties | yes | yes | yes |
| Which settings affect success? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Which prototype or item wins? | yes | yes | yes; without Session tags | yes; without Session tags | **partial**: Dynamic objects | yes; without Session tags |
| What predicts completion, churn, or return? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes; without Participant properties |
| Which UI surfaces are confusing? | yes | **partial**: Typed event properties | **no**: Typed event properties | yes | yes | yes |
| Which variant performs better? | yes | yes | yes; without Remote controls | yes; without Remote controls | yes; without Remote controls | yes; without Remote controls |
| What do users say? | yes | yes | yes | **no**: ExitPoll | **partial**: ExitPoll | **partial**: ExitPoll |
| Do shared-device users complete progression? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes; without Participant properties |
| How to prove compliance externally? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| What happened before quit/failure/crash? | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## Effort differences for the same recommendation

| Plan item | Unity | Unreal | visionOS | Android XR | WebXR | C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exit poll at end of module | low: place a prefab hook | low to medium: Blueprint nodes plus widgets and a Widget Interaction component | low: view model plus six shipped SwiftUI views, offline-capable | **verify support first** | **medium to high**: build the UI yourself | **medium to high**: build the UI yourself; voice answers possible |
| Track ten dynamic objects | low to medium | low to medium | medium: register each, upload each via web app | medium | medium | medium: register each, snapshot on movement, upload each via web app |
| Track spawned objects | ID Pool | ID Pool Asset | register per instance | register per instance | register per instance | register per instance with a custom id |
| Comfort / FPS / device metrics | free | add the components | mostly free, narrow set | FPS free, rest is your own sampling | partial | **all your own sampling** |
| Numeric event properties | free | free in C++, **broken in Blueprint** | **broken; put them on the session** | free, within 10 | free | free (JSON) |
| Eye-attention analysis | free on eye-tracked hardware | free on eye-tracked hardware | **impossible** | verify live | hardware dependent | only if the host supplies an eye-tracked gaze point; otherwise head direction |
| Offline operation | supported | supported | **supported and specified** | not documented | not documented | **none**; the host must persist failed requests |
| Install prerequisites | UPM | **project must be C++ based** | local Swift package, not a remote URL | Gradle plus AndroidX XR alpha alignment | npm, Node 20+ | C++11, an HTTPS client, source or CMake static library; pin a commit, there are no tagged releases |

## Screening rules

Apply these before presenting any plan:

1. **If the project is WebXR and not Three.js or Mattercraft, remove every dynamic object row.** Replace object-level gaze and interaction questions with custom events carrying an object identifier property, and state what that cannot answer.
2. **If the project is plain JS or any WebXR framework without dynamic objects, remove every per-object attention recommendation.**
3. **If the plan contains an exit poll, check the target supports one.** WebXR: scope the UI work. Unreal: scope the Widget Interaction component. **Android XR: verify ExitPoll exists at all.** visionOS and Unity: it is cheap, so place hooks early.
4. **If the plan contains remote controls, local cache, media, audio recording or multiplayer and the project is not Unity or Unreal, verify live before including them.** visionOS local cache is the exception: it is documented and solid.
5. **If the plan relies on biometric or device-level sensors, confirm the SDK and the hardware both support them.**
6. **If the project is anything but Unity, dev/prod separation is Phase 1 and non-negotiable.**
7. **If an objective uses a gaze or fixation step, confirm dynamic objects exist on that SDK.** On visionOS the objective will build and score, but it scores head direction: name it accordingly ("faced the notice", not "read the notice").
8. **Do not let `queryable_data.md` over-promise.** Its lists are written from the Unity SDK; where it and the tables above disagree, this file wins.
9. **If the project is Unreal, name the built-in component behind every comfort, performance, boundary or input metric**, and check the three that need hand dynamic objects.
10. **If the project is Unreal and any plan row carries a numeric property, state which authoring surface sends it.** Blueprint stringifies values.
11. **If the project is Android XR, count the properties on every event.** Ten is the cap and the surplus is dropped silently.
12. **If the project is visionOS or Android XR, confirm the asset pipeline can emit glTF Separate.** The Upload Web App rejects GLB, which is what most pipelines produce by default.
13. **If the project is visionOS and any plan row carries a numeric event property, move it to the session or accept the loss.** Custom event properties are string-only with no typed alternative.
14. **If the project is visionOS, restate every attention claim in the plan as head direction.** Then check whether the business question survives that restatement. If it does not, raise it during discovery rather than after the dashboard is full.
15. **If the project is C++, strike every "captured automatically" assumption, then ask two questions before anything else:** is the gaze point the host can supply eye-tracked or a head ray, and does the host's HTTPS layer behind `webRequest` retry. The first decides what every attention metric means; the second decides whether any data survives a bad network, because the SDK has no cache.

---

## When a team runs more than one SDK

Some organizations ship one experience to several targets: an engine build for headsets, a native build per platform, a WebXR build for the browser. Two things matter:

- **Event names, property keys and units should be identical across all of them.** They land in the same project and the same queries, and divergence splits every series permanently. Write the conventions document once and apply it everywhere (SKILL.md rule 3). Watch property **types** and **counts** especially: an event that is numeric on one SDK, stringified on another and capped on a third has effectively diverged three ways while looking identical in the plan. Design to the tightest constraint in the set.
- **Scene IDs and dynamic object IDs are per-project, not per-SDK.** If multiple builds report to one project, decide deliberately whether they share a scene or upload separate ones.

**One caution specific to mixed Vision Pro estates.** A team running a native visionOS build alongside a Unity build on eye-tracked hardware will have gaze data that means two different things under one property name. Either separate them with a session property that records the platform, or keep the analyses apart. Merging them silently produces an attention metric that is an average of two incompatible measurements.

Cross-engine background: https://docs.cognitive3d.com/scenarios/mixing-unreal-unity/
